clue.text: In many ways, it can help to reduce minor accidents

definitions.text: In many ways, it can help to reduce minor accidents

parts.words: In many ways, it can help to reduce minor accidents
parts.note: 'ways' are roads and 'minor' means under age: a road-safety rule taught to children to keep them from being knocked down

explanation.surface: A general remark that some all-purpose remedy cuts down on small mishaps.
explanation.walkthrough: The GREEN CROSS CODE is the British road-safety drill taught to schoolchildren (stop, look, listen); 'minor' points to the young pedestrians, not to small accidents.
explanation.definitionFit: The British children's kerb drill exists to prevent youngsters being hurt on roads.

clue.text: Remarkable formation of Ulster was a US agency involved with it?

indicators.note: involved suggests tangled up, so the letters of these words are rearranged together

explanation.surface: Asks whether an American agency had a hand in creating a famous Northern Irish landmark.
explanation.walkthrough: 'involved with' mixes the letters of WAS A US AGENCY together with IT. The GIANT'S CAUSEWAY is a coast of basalt columns in County Antrim, Northern Ireland.
explanation.definitionFit: The basalt columns of County Antrim are a famous natural geological feature in Northern Ireland.

clue.text: Profit from an adventure

definitions.meaning: to take advantage of or use for gain

explanation.definitionFit: To make use of something for gain, and, as a noun, a bold deed or escapade.

clue.text: Brass or steel

definitions.meaning: brass is slang for cheek or impudence
steel is firmness of resolve, courage

explanation.definitionFit: Both are words for boldness: cheek and courage.

clue.text: One who trains regularly should consider this a good deal

definitions.text: One who trains regularly should consider this a good deal

parts.words: One who trains regularly should consider this a good deal
parts.note: 'trains' looks like exercise but means travelling by rail; a frequent rail traveller gets a discount pass

explanation.surface: Advice that a keen athlete ought to think about some bargain.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain a RAILCARD is a discount card for rail fares, so a regular train traveller would find it a bargain.
explanation.definitionFit: A British discount pass on rail fares is a bargain for frequent passengers.

clue.text: Two sorts of evil character in Arabian Nights

parts.note: sin is one kind of evil
bad is another word for evil

explanation.surface: Two varieties of wickedness found in a figure from the Thousand and One Nights.
explanation.definitionFit: The sailor of the seven voyages is a hero of the famous Middle Eastern story collection.

clue.text: Weapons found in far from friendly nick, we hear

parts.note: cold means unfriendly

indicators.note: says the word for nick is spoken, and a word sounding the same is entered

parts.note: to nick is British slang for to steal

explanation.surface: Arms discovered in a police station that was decidedly unwelcoming.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nick' looks like a police station (British slang); it is the verb, to steal.
explanation.definitionFit: Bladed arms such as swords and bayonets are collectively called by this phrase.

clue.text: Force Spitfire to move in a circle

indicators.note: the circle is made to move into the other word, so it goes inside

parts.note: a spitfire is a fiery-tempered person, a dragon
a circle is shaped like the letter O

explanation.surface: Ordering a wartime fighter plane to fly in a loop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spitfire' looks like the fighter plane; here it is a fierce person, a DRAGON.
explanation.definitionFit: To dragoon someone is to coerce them into doing something.

clue.text: Falling over book left in buffet or bar, causing difficulty

indicators.note: these pieces go in, so the other word is wrapped round them

parts.note: to buffet is to strike, to sock
tumbling means falling over

explanation.surface: Someone toppling over at a buffet or bar and making trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'buffet' looks like a meal; here it is the verb to hit, SOCK.
explanation.definitionFit: An obstacle that hinders progress is exactly such a hindrance.

clue.text: Like individual I detained for slander

parts.note: as means like

indicators.note: detained means held inside, so the letter I is held within the other word

parts.note: a person is an individual

explanation.surface: A man held because of defamatory speech, like a single prisoner.
explanation.definitionFit: A damaging remark attacking someone's reputation is a slur.

clue.text: Was a jumper extremely loose fitting?

indicators.note: extremely points to the extremities, the first and last letters of loose

parts.note: apt means fitting

explanation.surface: Asks whether a pullover was very baggy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'jumper' looks like the British word for a sweater; it is one who jumps.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who jumped or sprang was acting as one who leaps.

clue.text: A peg before opening time

parts.note: a hole is an opening

explanation.surface: Something about a peg ahead of a pub's opening hours.
explanation.walkthrough: 'opening time' suggests when pubs open; it splits into a gap and a time letter. A THOLE is a pin in a boat's side for an oar.
explanation.definitionFit: A pin set in a rowing boat's gunwale serves as a fulcrum for the oar.

clue.text: First-rate opportunity to get place in college

parts.note: class as an adjective means first-rate
room means scope or opportunity

explanation.surface: An excellent chance to win a university place.
explanation.definitionFit: A teaching room is a space in any school or college.

clue.text: Nick drink and get arrested

parts.note: to nick is to make a small cut
a short is a small measure of spirits

explanation.surface: Someone steals a drink and ends up taken by the police.
explanation.walkthrough: 'arrested' looks like being taken into custody; it means halted.
explanation.definitionFit: Something halted before completion has been stopped early.

clue.text: In love with way one offers unconventional treatment

parts.note: in means at home
love is zero in tennis, the letter O
a path is a way

explanation.surface: A romantic way of describing an alternative medicine practitioner.
explanation.definitionFit: A practitioner of remedies based on tiny diluted doses works outside mainstream medicine.

clue.text: One chap joining another back in the doghouse

parts.note: Ken is a man's name

indicators.note: back means this name is read in reverse

parts.note: Len is another man's name

explanation.surface: Two men team up while one of them is out of favour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in the doghouse' suggests disgrace; the def is the dog's shelter itself.
explanation.definitionFit: A shelter for a dog is the literal meaning of the hut.

clue.text: Striking strings to make rough notes, perhaps

parts.note: workers striking are out
lines are strings or cords

explanation.surface: Musicians' strings being struck to produce rough musical notes.
explanation.definitionFit: Sketches or summaries give the main points without detail, as rough drafts do.

clue.text: Drop line to university, having been rejected the month before

indicators.note: rejected is read as thrown back, so the whole string is reversed

parts.note: to omit is to drop

explanation.surface: Someone dropped a line to a university but was turned down last month.
explanation.walkthrough: 'having been rejected' turns the whole of OMIT + L + U back to front.
explanation.definitionFit: In old commercial letters, the Latin term refers to last month.

clue.text: Old battleaxe making short work of silly man?

indicators.note: short means cut off at the end, losing its last letter

parts.note: a silly is a fool, a twit
Bill is a man's name

explanation.surface: A formidable old woman making quick work of a foolish man.
explanation.walkthrough: 'battleaxe' looks like a fierce woman; it is the weapon. A TWIBILL is a double-bladed medieval axe.
explanation.definitionFit: A double-headed axe of medieval times was a weapon of war.

clue.text: Report indicating gun was loaded?

definitions.meaning: a round inside the gun, split as two words

explanation.definitionFit: An official short news statement, and, split in two, a round placed in a weapon.

clue.text: Plant providing most of the fibre

indicators.note: most of means all but the last letter of the word

parts.note: istle is a fibre from tropical American plants

explanation.surface: A plant supplying the bulk of some fibre.
explanation.walkthrough: ISTLE (also ixtle) is a tough fibre from agave plants used in cordage.
explanation.definitionFit: The prickly Scottish emblem is a flowering weed.

clue.text: It holds food that's originally from South America

indicators.note: originally means the starting letter of the word

parts.note: Incan means of the Incas of Peru

explanation.surface: Some food originating in South America.
explanation.definitionFit: A metal container for preserved provisions keeps food fresh.

clue.text: Leader can take it ideal or otherwise

indicators.note: otherwise means arranged differently, so these letters are reordered

explanation.surface: A head of state may consider an idea or not.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Leader' looks like a person; it is a newspaper's leading article.
explanation.definitionFit: A newspaper's main opinion article is called its leader in Britain.

clue.text: Tory member's rise to the top

parts.note: C is short for Conservative, the Tory party
a limb is a member of the body

explanation.surface: A Conservative politician's ascent to power.
explanation.definitionFit: To ascend or scale upward is to go up a mountain.

clue.text: Boy has a pound in cash

indicators.note: in places the pound sign within the money word

parts.note: a coin is cash
L is the abbreviation for pound, from Latin libra

explanation.surface: A boy carries a pound in money.
explanation.definitionFit: A common male first name.

clue.text: In self-examination, about to reveal inner personality

indicators.note: about means turned round, so the concealed run is read backwards
in means the letters sit inside the word self-examination

explanation.surface: Self-scrutiny reveals one's true inner nature.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' picks AMINA from inside the word, and 'about' turns it round.
explanation.definitionFit: In Jungian psychology, the soul or inner self is the psyche's deep core.

clue.text: Painter with a fantastic talent is in business

indicators.note: is in places the rearranged letters within the business abbreviation

parts.note: CO is short for company, a business

indicators.note: fantastic means wild or fanciful, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An artist with extraordinary skill works in commerce.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fantastic' rearranges A TALENT into ANALETT, which 'is in' puts inside CO.
explanation.definitionFit: The Venetian view artist was an eighteenth-century painter.

clue.text: Call for Jacks in every round of cards possible with pack

parts.note: each round of a card game is a hand, so all of them are all hands
on means feasible, possible
a deck is a pack of cards

explanation.surface: A card game where all the jacks are summoned in each deal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jacks' looks like playing cards; it means sailors (jack tars).
explanation.definitionFit: A command summoning the entire crew to the ship's deck.
